title: "Experiment tracking"
subtitle: "Weights & Biases project layout for comparable runs"
---

# Shared project

All training scripts log to the W&B project named **`pokerai`**
(`pokerai.config.WANDB_PROJECT`).

| Run name | Trainer | How W&B is wired |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bigram-baseline` | `train_bigram` | Direct `wandb.init` / `wandb.log` |
| `gpt2-raw` | `train_gpt2` | Direct `wandb.init` / `wandb.log` |
| `gpt2-trl` | `train_trl` | `TrainingArguments(report_to="wandb")` |

This makes validation curves directly comparable in one dashboard.

# What gets logged

Typical configs include:

- architecture sizes (`n_layer`, `n_embd`, `n_head`, `n_positions`)
- vocab size / parameter count
- batch size, learning rate, epochs / steps
- device string
- train/eval example or pair counts
- masked-action-only flag (bigram)

# Login & offline modes

```bash
wandb login
# or disable entirely:
export WANDB_MODE=disabled
```

On air-gapped / batch compute:

```bash
export WANDB_MODE=offline
python scripts/train_gpt2.py
wandb sync wandb/offline-run-*
```

# Interpreting results

- **Bigram baseline** ≈ 1.53 val loss is the floor you must beat.
- Poker datasets are often **FOLD-heavy**. Raw CE loss can look strong while
  RAISE / BET quality remains poor—check action-type distribution from the
  converter / prepare step before over-interpreting.
- Prefer head-to-head comparison of TRL vs raw loop under identical data,
  tokenizer, and seed.
